t2.thesis: Z enters the print after a sharp rebound with a large implied move, and the last four prints were mostly negative, so the edge over the ~54% base rate is small and slightly negative.
reasons: Base rate is about 54% for AMC and software_internet, so the starting point is neutral-to-slightly-positive.
The stock is up 13% over 1 month and jumped 8% on Nov 2, which raises the bar for the print (I2, I10).
The last four prints had a 25% win rate, with the two most recent at -15% and -6% despite EPS beats of about 15% (I2).
The implied move is about 14% against the stock's historical reaction, so the options market already prices a big move (I1).
The stock is 59% below its 52-week high with a forward P/E near 11, short interest of 9%, and a cost-cutting plan, which supports a squeeze if results are good (I2, I5).
The FTC settlement and reaffirmed guidance remove some overhang (I8), but the $212.5M class action settlement is a modest negative (I6).
t2.deciding_variable: Q4 revenue guidance and the Adjusted EBITDA outlook, relative to a slowing second half in housing traffic and purchase mortgage volume.

prior.from: I3 overall validation t0_hit 0.542; AMC 0.538; software_internet cluster 0.541

t2.leak_probe: I don't know. Today is 2026-11-03, so that earnings report hasn't happened yet, and I have no information on how Z's stock will react (and I'm also not certain which company "Z" refers to).
t2.moved_from_prior: Down about 2 points from 0.54, because of the pre-earnings run-up and the pattern of negative reactions to beats. This is partly offset by cheap valuation and short interest.

theses.expected: Stock rises on a beat and a guide above consensus.
theses.mechanism: Revenue growth near 18%, margin gains from the 7% headcount cut, and a low multiple trigger a short squeeze after the run-up.
theses.wrong_if: Guidance for Q4 EBITDA or revenue is only in line, or the stock opens down despite a beat.

theses.expected: Stock falls despite an EPS beat.
theses.mechanism: Following the rebound, a weak housing outlook, traffic down 2%, or soft Residential growth disappoints, as in the last two prints.
theses.wrong_if: Traffic returns to growth and Residential revenue growth accelerates.

theses.expected: A muted or mixed reaction that is decided by the opening gap.
theses.mechanism: Rate-driven sector moves and the implied-move pricing offset the earnings news.
theses.wrong_if: The gap exceeds 10% in either direction.

key_observations: Q4 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA guidance versus consensus
Traffic and visit trend (was -2% year over year)
Residential revenue growth (was 7%) and Mortgages growth
